jurisdiction.name: Maldives
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: The Maldives has no AI law or national AI strategy yet: an AI masterplan announced by the President in 2024, an AI Act planned under the Maldives 2.0 digital programme and a Data Protection Bill before parliament were all pending in October 2026. The only published AI governance documents are the Prosecutor General's Office's August 2026 institutional AI strategy, AI governance framework and binding AI policy, which sets risk categories, prohibited uses and a ban on putting case data into public AI tools.
narrative.review_notes: This review was completed on 12 October 2026 and covers national law, government, ministries and regulators. The AI masterplan, planned AI Act and data protection bill are listed as leads. Not yet verified from the official text: material on the parliament and technology ministry websites.

instruments.issuing_authority: Prosecutor General's Office (Prosecutor General of the Republic of Maldives)
instruments.current_status: Version 1.0, August 2026, listed as 'In force' on the PGO 2.0 page (pgoffice.gov.mv). Launched by the President on 11 August 2026 (President's Office press release 2026-460). It applies only to the Prosecutor General's Office.
instruments.summary: The Prosecutor General's Office's own AI strategy and delivery programme (PGO 2.0) for 2026-2028, with a foreword by the President. It sets three pillars and six enablers to complete the Mafini case-management system and build eight governed capabilities into it (legal document analyser, Dhivehi-capable prosecutor assistant, summarisation and charge drafting, identity analyser, tamper-evident evidence, document exchange ledger, case intelligence and a citizen agent), on PGO-controlled infrastructure, with a two-year roadmap and results framework. It states fixed limits: no automated charging or discontinuation decisions, no PGO case data in public AI tools and no AI assessment of guilt or credibility from biometric features.

instruments.english_title: AI Governance Framework of the Prosecutor General's Office (PGO-FWK-AI-001)
instruments.issuing_authority: Prosecutor General's Office (Prosecutor General of the Republic of Maldives)
instruments.current_status: Version 1.0, date of issue August 2026, effective on issue, review within 12 months; listed as 'In force' on the PGO 2.0 page. Classification: public.
instruments.summary: Umbrella instrument issued by the Prosecutor General for governing AI at the Prosecutor General's Office, effective on issue. It sets nine governance objectives and nine principles (including non-delegation of human prosecutorial authority, confidentiality, court-facing transparency, accuracy, non-discrimination, auditability, contestability and risk-based proportionality, drawing on the UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI), maps the instrument set (strategy, policy, usage guides, AI tool register, controlled forms, standards alignment) and lays down rules of authority, conflict and amendment.

instruments.summary: The binding operational rulebook for AI use by Prosecutor General's Office staff, effective on issue. It assigns roles and decision rights (Prosecutor General, designated AI Lead, procurement and vendor management, data governance and IT security officers), classifies every tool by deployment category (approved PGO tools, enterprise tools, public tools that may never receive case information) and risk category (low, moderate, high, with committee review and Prosecutor General approval for high-risk uses), and lists absolute prohibited and restricted uses. It also covers the tool lifecycle and approval, data governance and data sovereignty, evidence and disclosure (including asking at intake whether AI was used), vendors, training, monitoring and audit logging, and incident reporting.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: The Maldives' official gazette, the President's Office, digital government sites, ministries and regulators were searched in Dhivehi and English. The Prosecutor General's Office AI strategy, framework and policy were found; there is no AI law and no data protection law yet, and no material was found for cybersecurity, transparency, standards, sandboxes, indices, drafts, international instruments or older publications (the pending data protection bill and an announced AI masterplan are leads). The data protection bill and the AI masterplan remain to be checked.

leads.title: Masterplan on the use of artificial intelligence (cabinet decision of 16 October 2024)
leads.issuing_authority: Ministry of Homeland Security and Technology with the Ministry of Economic Development and Trade
leads.note: President's Office press release https://presidency.gov.mv/Press/Article/31907 (cabinet meeting 16 October 2024) announced a masterplan covering AI risk management and a legal framework for AI. No official masterplan document was found on gov.mv sites on 2026-10-12 (the Ministry of Homeland Security and Technology site was unreachable through the proxy). Record when published.

leads.title: Data Protection Bill / Personal Data Protection Bill (People's Majlis, 2026)
leads.issuing_authority: Government of Maldives (submitted to the People's Majlis)
leads.note: Government bill reportedly accepted at first reading in June 2026 and referred to the Majlis Committee on Information and Communication Technology; would create a Privacy Commissioner. majlis.gov.mv returned HTTP 403, so the bill text was not read; not found in the Gazette as an enacted law on 2026-10-12. The Maldives 2.0 Pillar 4 milestones chart (https://digital.gov.mv/milestones/p4.pdf) lists 'PDPA Adopted'. Record as binding-law/data-privacy once enacted and gazetted.

leads.title: Artificial Intelligence Act (planned under Maldives 2.0)
leads.issuing_authority: Maldives Digital Service / Government of Maldives
leads.note: The official Maldives 2.0 Pillar 4 (Modern Legal Framework and Governance) major-milestones chart at https://digital.gov.mv/milestones/p4.pdf shows an 'AI Act Adopted' milestone (2026-2027 timeline). No bill text found; the chart has no AI policy content beyond the milestone and gives no publication date, so it is not recorded as a strategy instrument.

leads.title: Maldives AI Lab - National AI and Data Competency Centre (MINDCo and Bank of Maldives, launched May 2026)
leads.issuing_authority: Maldives Innovation and Digital Company (MINDCo) with Bank of Maldives
leads.note: Launched May 2026 under Maldives 2.0; the President's foreword to the PGO strategy says it aims to implement 25 AI use cases across the public sector by end of July 2028. No founding or governance document found on an official government site.

leads.title: Data Protection Bill (People's Majlis, 2026) - status update
leads.note: Update to existing lead: state broadcaster PSM/MMTV (22 June 2026) reports the Majlis approved the bill at first reading (66 votes) and sent it to the ICT Committee; would create a Privacy Commissioner. Not yet passed; no AI provisions reported. Official bill text on majlis.gov.mv not checked.
